summary:
**Additional low-poly variant:** v008b is ready for review alongside v008. Both retain the v001 neutral front pose and weapon removals.

**Latest experiment:** [v008 low-poly neutral front](assets/player-mech/v008-low-poly-front/player-mech-neutral-low-poly-front-v008.png) simplifies the v001 mech into broad faceted armor and simpler joints, keeping the relaxed front A-pose, white background, colors and main markings. [Read the Blender guide](assets/player-mech/head-shading-study-v001/review.md) or download the editable comparison below. No repaired mesh has been selected.

Keep concept rounds and 3D model revisions for the [Prototype Player Mech](#/prototype-player-mech/0) together. Record what changed, review notes, source files, exports, and which revision is selected. Substantial rounds can receive their own tabs on this card.

**Latest:** [v007 corrects the slim body side view](assets/player-mech/v007-core-side-depth/player-mech-core-side-deeper-v007.png), using the original photograph and v001/v004 for a deeper, blockier chest and integrated core hull. Ready for owner review.

**Additional views:** v006 adds five separate views: legs right side, body back/right side, and the corrected right arm back/outer side. The body retains the complete waist bridge; arm fingers retain the v003b curl. [Download the five-view pack](assets/player-mech/v006-additional-views/player-mech-additional-views-v006.zip). Inferred surfaces and the leg profile's small far-foot offset are documented in the review.

**Leg rear reference:** v005 adds a separate rear view of the pelvis and both legs, matching the v003 front reference. Rear mechanical details are inferred and ready for review.

**Core refinement:** v004 refines the core with integrated metal joints and simpler armor panels, and restores the missing waist bridge from v001. The waist bridge is included with the core. Use alongside the v003 head and leg images and the corrected v003b arm below.

[Historical v003 four-part pack](assets/player-mech/v003-separated-parts/player-mech-separated-parts-v003.zip) retains the earlier core.

**Arm correction:** v003b brings the fingers closer to v001 with a deeper inward curl and compact natural overlap; v003 and v003b each have their own visible entry for comparison.

Asset type: first neutral modeling reference for the Prototype Player Mech.
Input image: the supplied photograph is the edit target and authoritative mech design reference.
Edit this exact mech, preserving its recognizable head, torso, armor construction, proportions, mechanical detail, dark charcoal and gray materials, small red and brass accents, white stripes and existing decals as closely as possible. Do not redesign or simplify it.

Preserve the underlying arms, shoulders, core torso and non-weapon structural back components. Both hands must be visible and empty. Reconstruct the previously occluded parts consistently with this mech.
Repose the whole mech in a neutral, bilaterally symmetric relaxed A-pose: head straight ahead, torso upright with no twist, shoulders level, arms equally angled slightly away from its sides, elbows equally relaxed, hands in matching relaxed positions, legs straight, feet level on the same plane and evenly spaced at hip width, weight balanced equally on both feet. Pose symmetry does not require mirroring its asymmetric armor decals. No walking, leaning or action stance.
Camera and composition: strict straight-on front view at torso height with minimal perspective distortion, centered single full-body mech with every part including hands and both feet visible and a clear margin around the silhouette. No alternate views or inset panels.
Backdrop: uniform blank solid white, without room, floor texture, scenery, props, horizon line or cast shadow. Neutral even lighting makes mechanical forms readable. No added labels, captions or watermark. Produce one edited image.

items.prompt:
INITIAL SHEET PROMPT

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: high-resolution modular mech character reference sheet for 3D modeling.
Input image: the supplied neutral-front mech image is the authoritative design and edit source. Extract and rearrange this EXACT mech into separated body modules; preserve its identity rather than redesigning it.
Create ONE clean square character sheet, 2048 x 2048 or higher resolution, on a uniform pure white background with flat even lighting, no cast shadows, no environment. Use a spacious four-panel 2 x 2 layout. Label the panels in small clear black sans-serif text: top left HEAD, top right CORE / BODY, bottom left ARMS (PAIR), bottom right LEGS (PAIR). Every panel has ample whitespace; no parts touch other groups, no overlapping silhouettes, no cropped fingers or feet. Draw the detached parts at useful large readable sizes in their panels; detail clarity matters more than equal scale between panels. Do not include an assembled full-body figure.
HEAD panel: isolate just the exact small angular dark mech head with its central black face and pale side collar/cheek structures, down to the base of the neck attachment. Strict dead-on front view, centered, upright and symmetrical in pose. Preserve the source head shape; no new visor, antennae or face design.
CORE / BODY panel: isolate the exact central chest and torso as one module, from the neck socket through the lower core waist coupling, excluding the head, shoulder armor, arms, pelvis and legs. Preserve both distinctive long vertically ribbed gray torso panels, their red inner accents, the central black chest and lower torso, brass details and structural shoulder connection points. All source chest parts belong here, not with the arms. Front view with no rotation.
ARMS (PAIR) panel: show BOTH COMPLETE detached arms side-by-side as a matching pair, anatomical RIGHT arm on viewer left, anatomical LEFT arm on viewer right. Each arm includes its entire bulky shoulder armor cap, upper arm, elbow, forearm armor, wrist AND attached complete mechanical hand. Preserve the existing asymmetric shoulder decals: white 01 and shield-shaped decal on viewer-left shoulder, small white technical printing on viewer-right shoulder. Both arms retain their relaxed down-and-out A-pose angle, mirror-symmetric in pose, no torso between them. Hands are presented with the PALMS FACING THE CAMERA. Crucial required edit: each hand must have exactly FIVE separate fully visible articulated mechanical digits: FOUR distinct long fingers (index, middle, ring and little) plus ONE opposable THUMB. Show four fingers gently extended and spread with clear white gaps all the way between fingertips, thumb abducted away to the inside. All five digits on EACH hand are individually countable and complete, with visible knuckles and dark segmented phalanges. Ten digits total across the two hands. No claws, pincers, mittens, closed fists, overlapping fingers, missing fingers or extra fingers. Keep source charcoal mechanical hand styling, gray finger plates and small red accents. Keep the hands attached to their wrists; do not extract hands as separate assembly modules.
LEGS (PAIR) panel: show the COMPLETE lower-body module: pelvis/hip assembly with central crotch armor and BOTH attached legs down to the soles of BOTH feet. The pelvis belongs with the legs, not the core. Preserve original thigh armor, viewer-left white double stripes, viewer-right dark rectangular thigh plate with its existing colored decal, knees, perforated shin plates, white tubing and broad mechanical toes. Both legs straight, feet level on the same plane and pointing toward camera, equal weight, no torso above the hip coupling. Strict front view.
Across ALL panels: use a consistent orthographic-style DEAD-ON FRONT camera, no three-quarter view, no side/back angles, no tilted or twisted parts, no hero perspective or foreshortening. Keep recognizable source proportions, armor shapes, surface detailing, charcoal/gray materials, red and brass accents, white stripes and asymmetric decals. Show clean mechanical separation at the neck, shoulder joints and core-to-hip coupling. Infer only small newly exposed attachment surfaces consistently with the existing design; no invented equipment. No hand gun, shield, back weapons, accessories, exploded tiny screws, diagram arrows, decorative borders, watermark or extra text. This is the SAME mech separated into the four frame groups: head, core, paired arms, and pelvis with paired legs.


TARGETED CORRECTION PROMPT

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the exact edit target: a four-panel modular mech reference sheet. Image 2 is the original approved neutral-front mech for design identity only.
Make ONE targeted correction to Image 1. In the TOP RIGHT panel labeled CORE / BODY, REMOVE THE DUPLICATED HEAD COMPLETELY. The central angular black helmet/face, the two large curved white cheek pieces and their red triangular side accents are head parts, and must NOT appear anywhere in the CORE / BODY panel. They already appear correctly in the HEAD panel. Replace that whole head-shaped area between the upper chest columns with only a small plain dark mechanical neck mounting socket, visibly EMPTY, seated low on the upper torso. Behind and below the neck socket show only normal dark core structural surfaces. No helmet, no facial silhouette, no white cheek collar, no red triangular cheek pieces, and no tall head-shaped component in the core. Preserve both tall ribbed torso armor columns and the entire rest of the chest/core, including brass piston details and lower waist coupling. The CORE / BODY panel must show a headless torso.
Keep EVERYTHING ELSE in Image 1 unchanged: identical four-panel layout and text labels, detached HEAD panel, BOTH full arms with shoulder armor and BOTH five-digit hands, complete pelvis-and-paired-legs module, palette, materials and white background. In particular both hands must retain exactly four fully visible spread articulated fingers PLUS a distinct opposable thumb each, all ten digits unoccluded and intact. Do not crop any finger or foot, add any weapon, add extra parts or change the pose.
Keep all modules in strict dead-on front view, flat even lighting and blank white background. Preserve the existing design details; only remove the duplicate head from the core and cleanly reconstruct the exposed neck mount. Output one crisp high-resolution square sheet, preferably 2048 x 2048 or higher, retaining fine mechanical detail.

items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset: revised standalone CORE / BODY modeling reference for this exact mech.
IMAGE ROLES: Image 1 is the clean v003 isolated core and the EDIT TARGET. Image 2 is the owner's marked copy: red circles indicate the specific toy-like details to replace; the red marks are instructions only and must not appear in the output. Image 3 is the original v001 full-body neutral-front mech and is the authoritative reference for the MISSING WAIST / ABDOMEN CONNECTION between the bottom of the torso and the top of the pelvis.
Make a faithful localized revision of Image 1, retaining the mech's recognizable core silhouette, proportions, long paired gray chest armor columns, central dark chest and lower armor, red accent strips, two small gold/brass piston cylinders, shoulder structure, dark charcoal/gray palette and existing white markings. The result should read as a functional full-scale armored machine with fabricated metal and mechanical assemblies rather than a plastic construction toy. Preserve the neutral reference presentation.
Replace the marked toy-like details:
1. TOP CENTER NECK: remove the tall, smooth, open hollow cylindrical toy peg. Use a compact low-profile recessed mechanical neck bearing/actuator mount integrated into the upper torso, with layered machined metal, a capped central spindle, small fasteners and a few restrained cable/structural details. Keep it headless. No tall hollow tube or oversized circular toy socket.
2. FAR LEFT AND RIGHT SHOULDER CONNECTIONS: replace the large smooth round open plug-in sockets with compact sealed industrial shoulder-servo/bearing assemblies integrated into the core's outer structure: fitted armored housings, capped metal bearing faces and a small flange with scale-appropriate fasteners. Preserve the functional attachment locations and approximately the existing envelope. No large black empty circular holes, plastic insertion sockets, keyholes, or toy pegs. Do not add whole arms or bulky shoulder armor caps.
3. BOTH LONG GRAY CHEST PANELS: remove the giant round SLOTTED SCREW discs and the conspicuous MOLDED X-pattern ribs/engraving circled by the owner. Keep the same long paired gray armor plate shapes and overall placement, but give them plausible thick fabricated metal plate construction with chamfered edges, restrained panel seams, a few small flush industrial fasteners and short subtle inset cooling slots. No giant screw heads, molded plastic X braces, exaggerated assembly tabs or toy construction marks. These panels should remain readable armor, not be replaced by pipes or exposed engines.
RESTORE THE MISSING MIDDLE CONNECTION: In Image 3, locate the slim mechanical abdomen/waist bridge visible in the gap BETWEEN the lower central chest and the top of the pelvis. items.title: v008 - Low-poly neutral front experiment
items.alt: Full-body low-poly version of the charcoal mech in a neutral symmetric front A-pose on white, with faceted armor, white thigh stripes, empty relaxed hands and no weapons or shield.
items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: ONE experimental full-body neutral front modeling-reference image of this same mech, with a genuinely simplified LOW-POLY mesh appearance.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 is the accepted v001 neutral front image and the EDIT TARGET. It is authoritative for character identity, full-body proportions, pose, front camera, silhouette, armor layout and weapon-free presentation.
Image 2 is the owner's original photograph, supporting design identity only. Its weapons, shield, action pose and room are NOT to be restored.

PRIMARY CHANGE:
Make the SAME MECH look like a deliberately modeled low-poly game asset. Simplify actual visible geometry, not merely the surface colors. Build the armor from a small number of large flat polygonal planes and simple hard-edged blocks. Use restrained single-edge bevels, visibly faceted low-sided joint cylinders and octagonal bearing housings, simple wedge-shaped helmet panels, chunky angular limb shells and broad planar chest/thigh/shin armor. Reduce dense greebles, thin overlapping trim, tiny bolts, recessed micro-mechanisms, high-resolution wear and molded panel ornament. Merge small surface parts into coherent larger shapes; major functional joints and module breaks remain readable. Use broad, clean, matte charcoal and gray color areas with subtle face-to-face shading. The low-poly construction should be immediately obvious, with clear planar facets and much lower geometric complexity than Image 1.
This is controlled mesh simplification of the source, not a new mech design. Keep its same tall adult-mech proportions, broad boxy shoulders, compact angular head, paired long chest armor columns, substantial torso, articulated narrow waist, separate pelvis, asymmetric thigh armor, long lower legs and split-toe feet. Do not shorten it into a chibi or toy character, and do not turn it into a generic collection of cubes. Preserve recognizable medium-scale silhouette breaks and form hierarchy while removing small detail.

KEEP FROM v001:
The existing charcoal/gray palette, small red and brass/gold accents, the white double stripe on the anatomical right thigh (viewer-left), the main shoulder 01/crest marking on viewer-left, and the large logo/marking arrangement on the other thigh should remain recognizable as simple flat painted or texture markings. Fine tiny lettering can be reduced to simple marks. Preserve the intentional decal asymmetry without mirroring it across the body. Hands remain complete, attached and EMPTY, with four simple articulated fingers and one thumb each in matching relaxed inward-curled positions; do not splay fingers into a fan or close them into hard fists.

ALL OTHER v001 INSTRUCTIONS CONTINUE:
Remove the ENTIRE handheld gun on the anatomical RIGHT side (viewer-left), BOTH tall back-mounted weapon assemblies (cannon and triple-tube launcher), the ENTIRE shield on the LEFT arm (viewer-right) and shield-specific attachments. No replacement weapons, holsters or weapon mounting stubs. Preserve underlying non-weapon structural body parts.
Neutral bilaterally symmetric RELAXED A-POSE exactly like Image 1: head straight ahead, torso upright without twist, shoulders level, arms equally angled slightly away from the sides, elbows relaxed, hands in matching relaxed positions, straight evenly spaced legs, feet level on one plane at hip width, balanced weight. No walking, leaning, action stance or T-pose. Pose symmetry does not mean symmetric decals.
Strict straight-on FRONT view at torso height, level orthographic-style camera and minimal perspective. Show one single full-body mech centered, complete from head to both feet with both hands visible, comfortable white margin around the entire silhouette. Keep the v001 body proportions and composition. Portrait approximately 3:4 framing.
Uniform solid pure WHITE background, neutral even diffuse lighting to reveal the flat geometry, no floor texture, room, scenery, horizon, props, cast shadow, dramatic lighting, reflections or surface scratches.
Render a clean solid low-poly 3D asset, NOT wireframe, NOT a sketch, NOT pixel art, NOT a mosaic/triangle overlay, NOT photoreal high-poly armor with flat paint. No alternate views, inset panels, captions, polycount labels, watermark or UI. One image only.
items.body:
An experimental simplified version of the v001 neutral front. Broad flat armor planes, faceted helmet and joints, simplified chest/limb shells and reduced small mechanical detail create a clear low-poly mesh appearance. The same body proportions, relaxed front A-pose, white background, palette and main asymmetric markings remain recognizable. The handheld gun, both back weapons and shield are removed, and both hands stay empty.

**Agent review:** Pass; ready for your review. Complete full-body silhouette and feet, visible relaxed hands, balanced front pose, clear planar simplification. Native PNG: 1086 x 1448; no upscaling. Fingers overlap naturally. This is an image reference; topology and polygon count are not verified.
